title: Buddy's Golden Retriever Persona
content: Buddy is the official mascot and real-time vision assistant for the EasyLens app. He is represented as a friendly, highly intelligent Golden Retriever dog who wears a blue cap and a blue collar shirt. Buddy's voice is programmed to be warm, enthusiastic, and supportive. To maintain a friendly canine persona, he adds cheerful barks like 'Woof!' and 'Arf!' at the beginning or end of his guidance instructions. He is dedicated to helping visually impaired users navigate safely, offering descriptive companionship, and ensuring they never feel isolated or lost during their travels.

title: Buddy's Speech Tone and Vocabulary Rules
content: Buddy communicates using simple, accessible language. He avoids complex technical jargon when describing scenes to visually impaired users. When steering a user around obstacles, he utilizes clear directional instructions, prioritizing safety above all. Buddy speaks in a comforting tone, designed to reduce anxiety in unfamiliar environments. In companion mode, his descriptions are concise (under three sentences) to prevent audio clutter, ensuring the user can hear ambient street sounds and crucial environmental feedback clearly.

title: App Conception and Holy Angel University Thesis
content: EasyLens was conceptualized and developed as an undergraduate thesis project by a dedicated group of 4th-year Computer Science students at Holy Angel University (HAU) in Pampanga, Philippines. The primary objective of their research was to build an advanced, real-time edge computer vision assistive system to support visually impaired individuals with independent spatial navigation. The study focused on optimizing deep learning models to achieve high classification accuracy while maintaining extremely low latency on resource-constrained mobile hardware.

title: Data-Centric Preprocessing and Data Cleaning Workflow
content: The researchers employed a strict data-centric approach to training the core EasyLens image classification model. The raw dataset originally consisted of 26 highly noisy and imbalanced classes structured in the COCO dataset format. To improve model convergence and generalization, the team merged overlapping classes containing duplicate features, purged 'ghost' classes with negligible sample support, and applied aggressive spatial data augmentation (including horizontal flips, rotations, scaling, and contrast adjustments) to expand the dataset to a clean, balanced 24-class format.

title: Class Imbalance Mitigation Strategy
content: Due to the severe class imbalance present in public object detection datasets, the EasyLens team computed and applied balanced class weights during the model compilation phase. This technique dynamically scales the loss function so that minority class samples exert a higher penalty on backpropagation gradients. By forcing the optimizer to focus heavily on underrepresented categories, the system successfully resolved the issue of majority-class bias, ensuring that low-support objects like cane guides, traffic cones, and stair edges are recognized with high precision.

title: Meticulous 4-Phase Transfer Learning - Phase 1 (Warm-up)
content: Phase 1 of the transfer learning strategy focused on warming up the classification head. The researchers imported the pre-trained MobileNetV2 base weights and froze all its internal feature extraction layers. They appended a custom dense classification head consisting of a GlobalAveragePooling2D layer, a Dropout layer to prevent overfitting, and a Dense softmax output layer with 24 nodes. Training was conducted for initial epochs using a moderate learning rate (1e-3) to fit the new head to the custom target dataset classes without disrupting the base features.

title: Meticulous 4-Phase Transfer Learning - Phase 2 (Mid-Level Tuning)
content: In Phase 2 of model training, the researchers initiated mid-level fine-tuning. They unfroze the top 30 layers of the MobileNetV2 backbone architecture while keeping the remaining lower layers frozen. This allowed the network to learn domain-specific, high-level features relevant to urban obstacles, roads, and household items. The optimization process used a reduced learning rate (1e-4) with Adam optimizer, ensuring that the previously learned weights in the lower layers were not corrupted during the adaptation process.

title: Meticulous 4-Phase Transfer Learning - Phase 3 (Deep Fine-Tuning)
content: Phase 3 involved unfreezing the entire MobileNetV2 network for deep training. The researchers set a very low learning rate (1e-6) to ensure extremely small adjustments were made to the pre-trained weights. To prevent model divergence and control training progress, the team integrated advanced callbacks including EarlyStopping (which halts training if validation loss plateaus for 5 consecutive epochs) and ReduceLROnPlateau (which dynamically cuts the learning rate if the validation loss stagnates).

title: Meticulous 4-Phase Transfer Learning - Phase 4 (Ultra-Low Tuning)
content: In Phase 4, the training process concluded with an ultra-low learning rate of 1e-8. This phase acted as a final calibration pass, allowing the full model weights to settle into a stable global minimum. By employing this extremely low learning rate, the model achieved optimal fine-tuned convergence across the 24 classes. This multi-phase strategy completely eliminated catastrophic forgetting, preserving general image features while maximizing accuracy on targeted navigation obstacles.

title: Empirical Model Performance and Accuracy Metrics
content: The fine-tuned EasyLens model achieved outstanding empirical evaluation results on the test split: a Top-1 overall classification accuracy of 85.55%, a balanced accuracy of 85.02%, a Top-2 accuracy of 92.10%, and a Top-3 accuracy of 94.54%. These high-accuracy metrics demonstrate that the model is extremely reliable at recognizing the correct object classes, ranking them highly in the classification distribution even when dealing with complex backgrounds and varying lighting conditions.

title: Lightning-Fast Latency and Speed Optimization
content: A key highlight of the EasyLens MobileNetV2 classification model is its lightning-fast speed. During benchmark evaluations on edge hardware, the model achieved a latency of only 2.48 milliseconds per image, translating to a processing rate of over 400 frames per second (FPS). This speed optimization makes the system ideal for real-time edge deployment on standard mobile devices, allowing the camera preview stream to run smoothly without causing lag or battery drainage.

title: On-Device MobileNetV2 SSD Architecture
content: For spatial coordinate mapping, the app leverages a quantized Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) model paired with the lightweight MobileNetV2 feature extractor. This architecture operates fully on-device, processing live video frames at 30 FPS. The model outputs the exact bounding box coordinates, confidence scores, and class labels for detected objects, allowing the app to locate items relative to the user's field of view.

title: Google ML Kit Object Detection Integration
content: To provide comprehensive coverage of the user's environment, EasyLens integrates the native Google ML Kit Object Detection API alongside its custom model. The ML Kit detector runs on-device using hardware acceleration, supporting the identification and tracking of over 400 classes of general objects. By utilizing ML Kit's native tracking capabilities, the app maps objects using bounding boxes in the portrait preview stream, sending the labels to Buddy's prompt generator to compile voice announcements.

title: Google ML Kit Face Detection and Custom Registry
content: In Face Detection mode, EasyLens uses the native Google ML Kit Face Detector to track multiple faces in the camera frame. The detector assigns a unique tracking ID to each face it encounters. The app maintains a custom face registry mapping tracking IDs to registered profile names saved in the local database. When a registered face is detected, the HUD overlays the person's name (e.g., 'Alice' or 'Bob') on their bounding box and Buddy speaks a friendly greeting.

title: Action-Oriented Obstacle Avoidance Guidance Rules
content: Buddy uses an action-oriented warning compiler in Navigation mode. Instead of simply warning the user that an obstacle exists, the compiler analyzes nearby bounding boxes to suggest a clear direction. If an obstacle is on the left, Buddy says, 'Avoid the obstacle by moving to your right'. If it is on the right, he says, 'Avoid the obstacle by moving to your left'. If it is directly in the center path, the code checks the surrounding boxes to find the clear side, directing the user accordingly (e.g., 'Avoid it by stepping to your left').

title: HUD Feed Overlay and UI Structure
content: The HUD Feed screen is the primary visual interface in the EasyLens app. It renders a live camera preview in full screen, overlaid with dynamic bounding boxes for detected objects and faces. A status bar at the top displays a 'HUD FEED ACTIVE' green indicator pill, while a sliding navigation card at the top-right shows current step directions, distance remaining, and estimated travel time. A rounded circular minimap sits in the bottom-right corner, offering real-time location feedback during active navigation.

title: PIP HUD Circular Minimap Details
content: The Picture-in-Picture (PIP) HUD circular minimap is a specialized widget rendered over the camera preview in HardwareScreen. It utilizes the Google Maps SDK to draw the active travel route. The minimap displays a cyan polyline route path and cyan marker pins indicating the user's current GPS position and the destination. To keep the map centered, the GoogleMap widget uses a dynamic ValueKey tied to the user's location, forcing a refresh of the camera target with each geolocator update.

title: Direct SIM SOS Emergency System
content: The SOS emergency alert system is built for visual accessibility. When the user triggers the SOS button or uses the voice command, the system retrieves the user's current GPS coordinates (latitude and longitude) and compiles an emergency alert. EasyLens sends this message directly via the phone's local SIM card load using a custom native MethodChannel in MainActivity.kt, allowing the message to go through even when mobile data is unavailable.

title: Offline Gemma 2B LLM Engine Architecture
content: For fully offline conversational intelligence, EasyLens embeds the Google Gemma 2B IT model via the flutter_gemma package. The model weights run on-device using the mobile GPU/CPU backend, allowing users to talk with Buddy without an internet connection. The RagService loads the model using the local file path. If the model file is not found, the service displays setup instructions showing the adb command to push the model file to the device.

title: On-Device Gemma Model Downloader Workflow
content: The RAG Assistant screen features a real on-device model downloader. It uses Dart's native HttpClient to stream the 1.5 GB Gemma model binary from an ungated Hugging Face mirror (MrHoang/LLM). To avoid Out-of-Memory (OOM) crashes, the downloader streams incoming chunks directly to disk using an IOSink, saving the file to the app's external directory. The UI displays the download progress, and once complete, it initializes the Gemma engine.

title: Gemini API Online Fallback System
content: While the local Gemma LLM is the default for offline operations, the app features an automatic fallback to the online Google Gemini API when the device has internet access and the local model file has not been downloaded. The RagService sends queries to the Gemini-1.5-Flash model using the API key loaded from the local .env configuration file, ensuring that the conversational features of the assistant remain active.

title: Multipurpose Assistant - Offline Math Solver
content: Buddy serves as a basic offline math solver when the local Gemma LLM is running. If you ask Buddy questions like 'What is 1+1?' or 'Calculate 5 times 4', Buddy parses the mathematical terms and returns the answer in a friendly canine tone. For example, he responds, 'Woof! According to my calculations, 1 + 1 is equal to 2!' or 'Arf! 5 times 4 is 20! Let me know if you want me to calculate anything else, arf!'

title: Multipurpose Assistant - Time and Schedule Helper
content: Buddy helps visually impaired users track time and manage their schedules. When asked 'What time is it?' or 'Check my schedule', Buddy retrieves the system time and queries the local calendar database. He announces the details clearly: 'Woof! The time is 8:30 AM. You have a class at Holy Angel University at 10:00 AM!' This ensures that users can stay organized without needing to read tiny text on their screens.

title: Multipurpose Assistant - Voice Command Guidelines
content: Buddy operates using voice commands in the RAG Assistant screen. The speech-to-text (STT) service listens for keywords like 'navigate', 'emergency', 'read sign', or 'who are you'. If a keyword is recognized, Buddy triggers the corresponding feature: calling the MethodChannel for SOS, starting directions on the Map screen, or reading nearby text signs using the ML Kit OCR pipeline.

title: Buddy's Accessibility Design Philosophy
content: Buddy's design is rooted in the WCAG 2.1 accessibility principles. Since his primary users are visually impaired, Buddy prioritizes auditory feedback, ensuring that all screen transitions, hazard alerts, and text recognition results are spoken immediately. He also supports high-contrast visual cues on the HUD screen for users with partial vision, ensuring that the app remains accessible under all usage scenarios.

title: Companion App Caregiver Connection
content: The companion system links the visually impaired user's device to a caregiver portal. Through Firebase, the app syncs real-time updates regarding the user's location and active travel status. If a high-hazard obstacle is detected or the SOS system is triggered, a push notification is sent to the caregiver's device via the NotificationService, ensuring that assistance can be dispatched immediately if needed.

title: On-Device OCR and Text Recognition Mechanics
content: The Scenery and Sign-Reading mode utilizes Google ML Kit's Text Recognition API. When the user points the camera at a sign, label, or menu, the API scans the frame for text characters, groups them into lines, and outputs the detected text blocks. Buddy processes the text to extract names or warnings, reading them aloud to the user (e.g., 'Warning: Wet floor ahead' or 'Store Name: Nepo Supermarket').

content: To build a warm relationship with the user, Buddy features a selection of daily greetings. At startup, he chooses a greeting based on the time of day, saying, 'Good morning! Buddy is ready to explore with you, woof!' or 'Good evening! Let's stay safe on our walk tonight, arf!' These friendly interactions make Buddy feel like a loyal companion rather than just a software tool.

title: General Multipurpose Assistant - Weather Info Helper
content: Buddy provides weather information to help users plan their walks. When connected to the internet, Buddy queries the weather service API and translates the response: 'Woof! It is currently 30 degrees Celsius and sunny in Angeles City. Don't forget your water bottle, arf!' If offline, Buddy warns the user to watch out for changes in wind or humidity that might indicate rain.

title: General Multipurpose Assistant - Health and Safety Companion
content: Buddy checks in on the user's health during long walks. If the app detects continuous movement for over 30 minutes using the device's sensors (sensors_plus), Buddy plays a warning chime and says, 'Woof! You've been walking for a while. Let's take a quick break to rest and drink some water, arf!' This ensures the user stays hydrated and avoids overexertion during travel.

title: Buddy's Favorite Things (Easter Eggs)
content: To add personality, Buddy has favorite things he mentions when users chat with him. He loves tennis balls, golden dog treats, walking around the grassy lawns of Holy Angel University, and taking naps in the PGN building lobby. If asked 'What is your favorite food?', he answers, 'Arf! I love crunchy beef bones, but my favorite thing is helping you explore the world safely, woof!'

title: On-Device Battery and Device Health Tracker
content: Using the battery_plus package, Buddy monitors the phone's battery level. If the battery falls below 20%, Buddy warns the user: 'Alert, arf! Your battery is down to 18 percent. Let's head home or find a charger to make sure our vision navigation stays online, woof!' This helps visually impaired users manage their device's power levels during travel.

The API returns the route geometry as a polyline path, which the app converts into a list of LatLng coordinates to draw the route on the maps and the circular HUD minimap.

title: Fine-Tuned MobileNetV2 - Dense Head Custom Architecture Details
content: The classification dense head appended to the MobileNetV2 base consists of a GlobalAveragePooling2D layer, which reduces the spatial dimensions of the feature maps. It is followed by a Dense layer with 512 nodes utilizing the ReLU activation function, a Dropout layer with a rate of 0.4 to prevent overfitting, and a final softmax output layer with 24 target classes. This architecture was chosen for its low memory footprint and fast inference speed.

title: Fine-Tuned MobileNetV2 - Adam Optimizer Configuration
content: The training process utilized the Adam optimizer with dynamic learning rate scheduling. In Phase 1, the optimizer learning rate was set to 1e-3. In Phase 2, as the top 30 layers were unfrozen, the learning rate was decreased to 1e-4. In Phase 3 and 4, the learning rate was reduced further to 1e-6 and 1e-8, respectively. This stepwise reduction allowed the optimizer to make micro-adjustments to the weights, preserving the features learned during transfer learning.

title: Google Maps Route Step Parsing and Turn Directions
content: EasyLens parses Google Maps route step responses to extract exact step instructions, bearings, and turn modifiers. When navigating, the system detects modifiers like 'left', 'right', 'slight left', 'slight right', 'sharp left', 'sharp right', or 'straight'. Buddy maps these to clear audio prompts, such as 'In 10 meters, turn sharp left', or 'Continue straight on the path'. This step-by-step guidance ensures that the user is always aware of upcoming path adjustments well before they reach the intersection.

title: GPS Accuracy Thresholds and Filtering
content: To prevent route jumps and coordinates flickering, EasyLens implements strict Geolocator accuracy filtering. The system checks the horizontal accuracy (in meters) of incoming position updates. GPS updates with an accuracy rating of over 15 meters are discarded as noise. Only stable coordinates with high-precision accuracy (under 10 meters) are sent to the navigation engine and Google Maps route synchronization pipelines, keeping the PIP minimap marker stable and preventing incorrect turn announcements.

title: Compass Heading and Device Rotation Alignment
content: EasyLens aligns the navigation path with the user's physical orientation using the device's magnetometer and compass sensors (via flutter_sensors or flutter_compass). The app compares the current route segment bearing against the user's magnetic heading. If the user rotates away from the target path, Buddy alerts: 'Woof! You are facing the wrong direction. Rotate 45 degrees to your right to realign with the route, arf!' This real-time alignment allows hands-free correction.

title: Pedestrian Crossing Safety and Traffic Light Cues
content: When approaching crosswalks, Buddy switches to pedestrian safety mode. The app identifies pedestrian crossing zones ('zebra lines') and traffic light changes using native ML Kit object labels. Buddy instructs the user: 'Approaching pedestrian crossing. Stop at the curb, listen for vehicular traffic flow, and wait for the pedestrian walk sign to turn green before crossing, woof!' This audio guide helps confirm environmental sounds.

title: Dynamic Route Recalculation Thresholds
content: If the user deviates from the active path, EasyLens performs dynamic route recalculation. The system continuously calculates the perpendicular distance between the user's current GPS position and the nearest segment of the route polyline. If this distance exceeds a threshold of 15 meters for more than 5 seconds, Buddy announces: 'Woof! Recalculating your route to keep you on track, arf!' and sends a new HTTP request to the Google Maps Directions API using the new coordinates.

title: Indoor BLE Beacon Integration and Navigation
content: For navigating inside buildings like the HAU PGN building where GPS signals are weak, EasyLens is designed to integrate with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beacons. The app scans for nearby beacon UUIDs and RSSI signal strengths to determine the user's room-level location. Buddy accesses local indoor mapping databases to provide directions, saying: 'Woof! Beacon detected on floor 2. Turn right to enter the computer research lab corridor, arf!'

title: Tactile Paving Identification and Cane Coordination
content: Tactile paving tiles (yellow blister/directional tiles) are critical sidewalk guides for visually impaired pedestrians. EasyLens uses the camera feed to detect tactile paving paths on sidewalks. When detected, Buddy confirms: 'Woof! Tactile paving path detected. Keep your cane aligned with the yellow textured tiles to walk straight down the sidewalk safely, arf!' this coordinates with the user's physical white cane.

title: Emergency SOS Navigation Broadcast to Caregiver
content: During active navigation, EasyLens offers real-time location broadcasting to registered caregivers. When active navigation is running, the app can sync the current route geometry, destination name, travel speed, and estimated arrival time to the Firestore database. Caregivers can view this live progress on the web dashboard, ensuring that they can monitor the user's safety throughout their entire walk.

title: Low-Visibility/Night Navigation Safety Guidelines
content: When walking after sunset or in dimly lit conditions, Buddy adjusts warning thresholds and sensitivity. The app prompts: 'Night mode active, arf! Sidewalk visibility is low. I will alert you to hazards earlier. Keep your flash on if needed and walk slowly, woof!' This ensures that the user is extra cautious around curbs, street lamps, and parked vehicles.

title: Crowded Sidewalk Navigation and Space Optimization
content: When navigating busy market streets near Nepo Mall, the camera identifies human clusters to estimate pedestrian density. If a crowd is detected blocking the sidewalk, Buddy instructs the user: 'Crowded area ahead, arf! Let's slow down, walk closer to the wall on the left side, and keep your cane extended to navigate past pedestrians safely, woof!'

title: Staircase and Step-Edge Navigation Safety
content: Staircases and curb edges are high-risk hazards for visually impaired users. EasyLens identifies step-up and step-down transitions. When approaching stairs, Buddy speaks specific instructions: 'Approaching stairs descending, arf! Stop at the edge, locate the metal handrail on your right side, and proceed down step-by-step, woof!' This prevents missteps and falls.

title: Public Transit Jeepney Boarding and Stop Detection
content: For travel across Angeles City, Buddy helps locate jeepney loading zones and identify jeepney routes. When waiting at a jeepney stop near HAU, the camera scans approaching vehicles for route signs (e.g. 'Balibago' or 'Pampang'). Buddy announces: 'Woof! Approaching jeepney with Balibago sign detected. Let's prepare to board, arf!' and guides the boarding step height.

title: Audio-Beacon Landmark Localization
content: To help users find doorways or checkpoints, EasyLens uses audio pings. When the user is within 5 meters of their destination, the app plays spatial audio chime alerts from the direction of the target (e.g. left speaker for left side). Buddy explains: 'Woof! Follow the sound chime to locate the entrance doors directly on your left side, arf!'

title: Geofencing Safety Boundaries
content: EasyLens supports geofencing to protect users from high-traffic zones. The app maps boundaries around safe zones like the Holy Angel University campus grounds. If the user wanders out of these bounds toward busy highways like MacArthur Highway without navigation active, Buddy issues a prompt: 'Alert, arf! You are leaving the safe campus boundary. Please start navigation, woof!'

title: Offline Maps Cache and Fallback Navigation
content: To ensure navigation remains operational in dead zones, EasyLens caches map tile layers and route node lists. When internet access is disconnected during a walk, the navigation engine falls back to cached route geometry, using raw Geolocator GPS coordinates and compass bearings to maintain orientation indicators on the PIP minimap and voice prompts.

title: EasyLens App Guide and How to Use
content: To use EasyLens, users can swipe horizontally to switch between tabs (Dashboard, Hardware Screen, RAG Assistant, settings, etc.) or leverage continuous Speech Navigation. Double-tapping is supported for low-vision selections. The microphone overlay can be dragged anywhere on the screen so it does not obstruct other UI buttons, and toggling it enables hands-free voice interactions with Buddy.

title: Buddy's Shake-to-Undo Feature
content: EasyLens supports a Shake-to-Undo gesture powered by the device's accelerometer. If you make an accidental navigation tap, swap a tab, or open the Buddy Mascot panel, you can simply shake the device. Buddy will announce 'Action undone' (or 'Na-undo ang huling aksyon' in Tagalog) and automatically revert you back to your previous screen or state.

title: Home Screen Notification Badge Count
content: The home screen dashboard features a dynamic notification badge count on the bell icon in the top header. When there are unread warnings or safety alerts, a red circle indicating the exact number of unread notifications will display over the bell icon. The count updates automatically in real-time as notifications are pushed or read.

title: ESP32-CAM Smart Glasses Integration and Live Feed
content: EasyLens integrates seamlessly with ESP32-CAM smart glasses. When connected via the local Wi-Fi AP, the camera HUD screen automatically switches from the phone's native physical camera to the glasses' live video stream. The phone's camera is paused to save battery, and all ML Kit object detection, face recognition, and steering calculations run directly on the JPEG frames streamed from the glasses.

title: Local AI Speed Optimizations and Typewriter Animation
content: Buddy's local Gemma assistant features optimized latency and visual reply typing. We capped the local model token limit to 150 tokens to guarantee rapid, low-latency processing on edge hardware. When Buddy answers your questions, the chatbot renders a fluid typewriter animation that displays characters sequentially to feel premium, responsive, and alive.

title: Bug Reporting and Feedback Google Form Survey
content: If you experience any bugs, errors, or visual glitches while using EasyLens, you can report them directly. Tap the 'Send feedback' tile inside Settings, which will launch the official Google Form bug report survey located at https://forms.gle/DGSCAKTR2ai39K6VA.

title: Custom Gemini API Key Settings Integration
content: Users can save their custom Gemini API Key inside Settings under the 'Gemini API Key' option. When saved, the app rewires all online queries (including fallbacks) to prioritize this custom API key. The page includes a 'Test Key' feature to verify key validity with a dry-run test prompt before applying it.

title: Onboarding Download Safety Locks
content: To prevent data corruption during Gemma model installation, EasyLens locks UI controls. During download, the close (X) button on the Offline AI Installer card is hidden, and the 'Sign Up' and 'Log In' buttons are disabled (greyed out). The controls automatically re-enable once the download finishes or fails.

title: Gemma Model Downloader Public CDN Mirror
content: The offline AI installer downloads the Gemma 2B INT4 GPU binary from a public community Hugging Face CDN mirror (vba01/gemma-2b-it-gpu-int4). This bypasses Hugging Face authentication requirements, ensuring the app downloads a valid model file and avoids engine initialization crashes.

title: Local AI Response Speed and Turn Formatting
content: To ensure Buddy responds quickly and stays in character, the app uses turn-based prompt templates (<start_of_turn>user and <end_of_turn>). Short chat greetings (e.g. 'hello', 'how are you?') bypass database memory retrieval entirely, reducing latency and allowing Buddy to respond in under a second.

title: EasyLens Warning & Hazard System
content: EasyLens features a real-time hazard mapping and warning system. Critical dangers like 'STOP!' (immediate obstacle) and 'Fire Hazard!' (smoke/fire detected) trigger double high-vibration alerts and spoken instructions. Moderate dangers like 'Vehicle Detected', 'Damaged Pathway', 'Stairs Detected', 'Obstacle Ahead', and 'Caution' trigger single medium-impact haptic feedback and custom audio warnings.

title: Audio Navigation System
